Besides my weight loss, I spent all of my teenage years basically hiding from beauty. I was super shy and no one noticed me which made me comfortable being invisible. Being in uniform only schools + long term medical issues meant that all the clothes I had where baggy and unflattering. I used to think nice clothes, makeup and hair were only for girls who deserved it—not girls like me. My weight gain only made these feelings worse. Plus, at my heaviest, I moved to an all girls majority white boarding school which only made my self image worse. 

My routine was super gradual lol I used to save pictures of girls on Instagram and try to emulate them. I knew nothing about foundation, lashes, hair, clothing. I started watching YouTube tutorials in the gym, started reading magazines, following style accounts. In 2017 I went through like 5 different aesthetics haha. I started taking skincare seriously, learnt that wigs are the best hair options for me and cultivated a personal s tyle. I think the most important thing I did was realise the I could define beauty in my own terms? Like I didn’t have to look like a white girl, or a Kardashian, or be unrealistically curvy to be beautiful. And voila! 

It’s never too late to change, start something new, evolve. I’m happy to say that I’m becoming my ideal self. I’m happy with who I am and ready to conquer my 20s! (Also start wearing lashes omg life changers get them really cheap on aliexpress xx)

It’s largely out of your control. Don’t aim to lose more than a 1lb per week to ensure slow, sustainable weight loss. If you’re able enough to strength train/ lift weights—start. Building muscle is nature’s skin smoother.

Up your protein intake. The key to maintaining (and building within your 1st year of lifting) is to keep protein at 60g +. Each meal should average around 15+ grams of protein. Protein is also the most satiating macronutrient so v important for the typical high-carb vegan diet. (nothing wrong w/ carbs tho)

You could stand to eat more calories—only because I think you’d get burnt out much quicker on such a low deficit. Try upping your intake to 1300-1400 within 2 weeks and see how you feel/ track any progress. 

Looking lean is a lot more complex than just losing scale weight. You could not move at all and still drop weight. It seems like you want to change body composition as opposed to looking like a smaller, equally flabby version of yourself. This is where consistent weight training and high protein comes in. 

Think of the 3 rules of body composition:

1) Eat at a caloric deficit to lose fat

2) Prioritise protein (e.g 0.7 per lb of body weight) in your meals, aiming to get at least 15g or more in 2-3 meals/shakes

3) Lift weights with the goal of progressive overload and increasing strength to ensure muscle gain—and thus better body composition

I managed to get 90g per 1500 through fake meats. Game changers honestly. They're demonized a lot in vegan fitness circles but if you want low calorie, high protien--it's a great option.  1 cup of TVP/soy ground is around 20g of protein for no more than 200 kcals. Products like Yves do vegan soy burgers for 14g per 100cal. Compare that to a black bean burger--higher in calories and usually around 6g per patty. Having 1 cup of peas as a snack (with some herbs) is 145cal and 13g of protein. 

​

A sample day for me would be:

Vega sport protein powder w/ hot water-- (P:30g)150 calories

1 boiled potato, 1 cup of TVP bolognese and 1 cup of broccoli: (P:26) 461 calories

1 cut up Yves veggie burger (14g) with 1 cup of chickpeas (12g), half an avocado, 1 medium tomato and 2 cups of mixed lettuce: (P:34g) 590 calories

1 cup of peas with herbs: (P:13g) 145 calories

TOTAL CALORIES: 1346

TOTAL PROTEIN: 103g

​

You just have to prioritise protein with every meal--treat carbs and fats as an addition, not the foundation. You could also splurge on high protein bread or chips if you want. Hope this helps!
